classification.difficultyReason: Combines intersecting-chord, tangent–secant, equal-tangent and secant-product rules to determine four lengths.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Two tangents and two secants from one external point; the lower secant intersects a chord ending at the lower tangent contact. Ordinary source pink and teal strokes are replaced by black house geometry. Coordinates derive tangency, circle intersections and the crossing topology from the supplied lengths; no auxiliary construction labels are printed.
spec.mathematics: Lower secant: external length 8 cm, internal portions 6 cm and 4 cm. Crossing chord: portions x and 3 cm. Upper secant: external length 9 cm and internal length z. Upper and lower tangent lengths are y and w.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens and unknown labels are visible; the printed teacher answers are omitted.

answer.short: $w=12\text{ cm},\ x=8\text{ cm},\ y=12\text{ cm},\ z=7\text{ cm}$
answer.worked:
Intersecting chords have equal products of their intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}3x&=4\times6\\3x&=24\\x&=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The square of a tangent equals the product of the external secant length and the whole secant length.
$$\begin{align*}w^2&=8(8+6+4)\\w^2&=144\\w&=12\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Tangents from the same external point are equal, so $y=12\text{ cm}$.

Secants from the same external point have equal products of their intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}9(9+z)&=8(8+6+4)\\81+9z&=144\\9z&=63\\z&=7\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
